correctness.rationale: The four characters and p−1 inequivalent two-dimensional irreducibles exhaust 4p by the sum-of-squares identity. In the two-dimensional blocks the off-diagonal term of M* M is (1+(−1)^k) times the product of two conjugate tap sums, while both diagonal entries equal the sum of squared magnitudes. This gives the claimed parity-dependent singular values, with each block repeated twice. For odd k cancellation in either coordinate is exactly antipodality; for even k equality of magnitudes is exactly r=±s mod p, and neither even magnitude can vanish. Together with the character zeros this gives the nullity formula. The separation weights are 2p unless antipodal (p). Nonexceptional resonances have total weight 8p²(p−1), of which 2p²(p−1) have both separations odd; subtracting these and (p,p) from the both-odd weight p^4 and then taking the complement gives the two nonresonant rows, with the 3/p collision at p=3. The minimum positive even difference is twice the unique first cosine gap. When neither separation is antipodal, the odd-sector bound uses two positive terms, so it is strictly above that gap even at p=3. When exactly one separation is antipodal, invert the other separation mod p and use its representative up to sign to realize the first cosine gap. When both are antipodal the only positive singular value is 4; otherwise k=1 gives a positive value strictly below 4. The constant vector and triangle inequality give norm 4.

The exact nullity census and equality classes resolve a substantive stability question: the largest kernel occurs when all surviving modes are perfectly conditioned, whereas worst conditioning grows quadratically in p and is possible with just the unavoidable one-dimensional kernel. The distinction matters on the recoverable subspace only.
